title: Emergency Measures
subtitle: One must have the wisdom to adapt to endless change in the face of what never changes.

trails.title: "New Faces, Old Friends"
trails.description: Those still fresh—and those you've grown tired of.

content.text:
[A flowing handwritten note; faint scale powder clings to the paper.]

Taira
His true form is a crab that latches onto the faces of others. Through his arcane skills, he can control the movements of his host. The death of the host does not harm him. Always be wary of the crab.

Lyra
She can control—or amplify?—emotions through song. Her voice is highly mobile, and her wind-based arcane skills are wide-reaching and difficult to guard against.

Ustrina
The medium of her arcane skills is possibly a shadow in the shape of a sickle. She can use it to inflict mental damage, though her victims show no visible physical wounds or signs of pain. Evade the sickle, and use mental defense arcane skills if possible.

Hypothetik
He takes the form of a giant stitched puppet. His arcane skills allow him to implant emotions, beliefs, or fragments of consciousness into the minds of others—most commonly fear. Counter him the same way you would against Ustrina.

İlmek
No arcane skills have been observed, but her strength and endurance far exceed ordinary limits. Avoid engaging her up close.

Prima
Skilled in hypnosis and torture, and known for her brutal nature. Her mother, Animus, was a Manus Apostle and died during the Antarctic incident.

...

No deeper contact has been made with the remaining leaders. Physical descriptions of suspected leaders are recorded in the appendix.

items.text: Emergency Measures
Countdown to the "Storm"
Courtroom

items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: Warning: Stage one alert. Unidentified intruders in headquarters. Emergency evacuation procedures initiated.

items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: All personnel are to obey ranking officers during evacuation and await further instructions in the emergency shelters.

items.speaker: Broadcast
items.text: This is not a drill. Repeat: Stage one alert. Unidentified intruders in headquarters.

items.speaker: Special Tribunal Officer
items.text: Quiet in the court. The trial will not be interrupted.

items.speaker: Special Tribunal Officer
items.text: The Foundation's security forces are more than capable of handling whatever emergency is occurring outside. This tribunal is perfectly safe.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: Your Honor, might I suggest a recess until the end of this crisis? There are a number of critical personnel gathered here.

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: I have no doubt our security forces are capable, but without senior leadership to direct them, chaos is inevitable.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: We must evacuate to the nearest emergency shelter immediately and wait for rescue. As the ranking officer, Your Honor, you are in command of the evacuation.

items.speaker: Special Tribunal Officer
items.text: You're right.

items.speaker: Special Tribunal Officer
items.text: In that case, I declare a recess until the end of this present crisis. During this period, the defendant shall remain in custody. Other personnel will return to their positions and—

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: You're going to get people killed!

items.speaker: Special Tribunal Officer
items.text: Mr. Creius, I would remind you that any statements you make will be on the record when the court returns to session.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I know, but I'll say it anyway. Because I know the truth is on my side, Your Honor.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Listen to me, everyone. Forget the procedures. If the Manus are brazen enough to attack us at our headquarters while the "Storm" is imminent, then they must have come with overwhelming force.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: We'll need all personnel and every asset to resist this assault. If we can concentrate our defenses here, the long and narrow corridors of the Committee Building can work to our advantage.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: This will be a fight for our lives.

items.speaker: Special Tribunal Officer
items.text: Mr. Creius, what evidence do you have that this "assault" is beyond what is already accounted for in our emergency procedures?

items.speaker: Irinei
items.text: Indeed. You're a former Vigil, Creius; you should be well aware that there is simply no teleportation array with the capacity to move such a force into our security perimeter undetected.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Have you already forgotten our investigation into Hill 299? They hollowed it out and transferred ten thousand soldiers inside without being noticed.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: We cannot rule out that Manus Vindictae now possesses some form of stealthy, high-capacity teleport array. We all but confirmed it following their movement patterns during the Don Operation.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: There's a decent chance this assault is stronger than our protocols can handle. We have to mobilize everyone—anyone who can stand needs to be a part of this fight.

items.speaker: Pedra
items.text: Including our civilian staff? They don't know the first thing about combat! This plan of yours could only result in needless death.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I'm not asking for them to pick up a rifle. They'll set up barricades, run messages, care for the wounded—anything they can do to help.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: We have a hall full of soldiers, veterans of this era's battle against Manus Vindictae, all prepared to sign our military service contract. They could be the key to organizing a counterattack, if they aren't already in the fight.

items.speaker: Special Tribunal Officer
items.text: Even if we agreed to execute your plan, no one present has the authority to command it.
There's static over the loudspeaker, then a calm female voice, so calm it seems as if it must be a pre-recorded warning.

items.speaker: Special Broadcast
items.text: Attention: This is an official Presidential Office broadcast. Emergency evacuation procedures are canceled. All combat personnel to battle stations.

items.speaker: Special Broadcast
items.text: Non-combatants in distress, prepare to resist within safe limits.

items.speaker: Special Broadcast
items.text: The Pre-Storm Dispatch Center takes command of all units, effective immediately. Any personnel unable to reach safety or receive direct orders are permitted to resist by any means available. There will be no liability assigned for any damage to headquarters sustained during resistance efforts.

items.speaker: Special Broadcast
items.text: May the peace be with us.
Battle stations—an unprecedented situation for headquarters. Across the sprawling complex, staff begin to organize.

items.speaker: Special Tribunal Officer
items.text: May the peace be with us.
The Special Tribunal Officer aims to be the first to the door, but Creius is faster, eager to take the opportunity to leave.
A tiny yet shrill screech rings in Ms. Stranger's ears. In the end, however, it's drowned out by a wave of other noises.
Room, St. Pavlov Foundation

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Ugh!
It feels as though her ears are bleeding. Fortunately, when she raises a hand to check, she finds it to be only sweat.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: How did I get here?
She tilts her head back. It offers some relief from the tinnitus.
Now, her senses are overwhelmed by the cries coming from outside the corridor, gunshots, and incantations.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Arcana didn't kill me. What did she ...?
She presses her temple. She feels it—something massive yet hollow swelling inside her skull, enveloping her thoughts in the blackest of nights.
Ms. Stranger! You're awake.
Someone reaches out to help her up.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Are you okay? Any pain?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Ah, Eagle?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Yes, I'm fine, I think. But how did we end up here?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I got separated from Ms. Marguerite in the assault. The Manus captured the first floor before I could reach the emergency shelter.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: I was running along the hallway and found you passed out on the floor. Luckily, a guard saw us and helped me move you here.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: We're safe here. Well, for now.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Thank you, Eagle. What about the guard?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: He ...
Eagle looks over to a guard lying in a heap along with a Manus soldier. Both are dead.
A damaged mask lies at Ms. Stranger's feet.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: We need to go.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But where, Ms. Stranger?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Somewhere—anywhere else. It's too dangerous to stay here.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: If they've secured the first floor, then they've likely already begun searching it room by room for survivors.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But there are so many of them out there. We can—
She spots the mask in Ms. Stranger's hand.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Please don't put it on, Ms. Stranger.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It'll deceive the Manus soldiers. I'll use it to find a way out for us.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Don't worry. The Foundation's headquarters was designed as a military fortress. There are plenty of hidden shelters around. We'll find a safe place.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: But once we're out in the open, it'll be just the two of us against all of them. The Scout Code would say that we should hold in place and wait for rescue.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The battle is still raging. Even if they've managed to hold the line somewhere, it's unlikely they'll be sending rescue teams any time soon.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Hmm? Ms. Stranger?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Manus Vindictae could find this room at any time. We can't stay here.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I promise I will get you out of here, Eagle. You wouldn't have been trapped if you hadn't saved me.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: It's not your fault, Ms. Stranger. I made that decision myself.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I know. It's just ...

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I can't shake the feeling that I'm to blame. I must have missed something, some detail that could have helped us foresee this attack.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I need to make up for this mistake, even if all I can do is save one life.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: We need to go. Now.
Ms. Stranger is once again her calm, collected self. She's still holding the mask. Black globs of liquid drip from it.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Are you really going to put it on?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Only when I have to. I need a disguise if I'm to avoid combat.
There they are!
Wait! She's got a mask in her hand.
Watch out! There's a kid, J.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Oh, sorry. I figured you were one of them.

items.speaker: J
items.text: You don't need that mask anymore. So, would'ya mind dropping the thing?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Understood.
She does precisely as he asks.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Phew. Thanks.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: I knew I'd find you here.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Ma'am!

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: You didn't lose the badge I gave you, even when you were in danger. Nicely done.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: That badge was enchanted by X to emit a special kind of arcane trace that my Rumbling Roaring Box could identify, but I lost the thing in battle.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Thankfully, despite most of these checkered doormats being about as useful as a flat tire, they do carry monitoring devices capable of picking up those traces, so ...

items.speaker: J
items.text: Wait, you put a tracker on this kid?

items.speaker: J
items.text: *sneer* Not cool, lady.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Technically speaking, it's only an arcane trace emitter.

items.speaker: J
items.text: Ugh, never mind. At least everyone's okay.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I thought the first floor was fully under Manus Vindictae's control. How did you manage to get to us?

items.speaker: J
items.text: Well, when all this s**t went down, we decided to swing by the Arcanum Containment Department. Found this weird screaming box there. Turns out it works pretty good as a distraction.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Ms. Druvis managed to evacuate most of the survivors to the Arcanum Containment Department in the Eastern Building.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: The Manus have focused their efforts on reaching the top level of the Committee Building.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The top level? They must be heading for the president's office.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: We can't worry about that now. We have our own problems.

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: Agreed. Let's fall back to the Arcanum Containment Department. We'll make our next plans there.
Arcanum Containment Department

items.speaker: "Razor"
items.text: This is all the men we could gather so far.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: You've found more survivors, Captain.

items.speaker: Name Day
items.text: Then it's not all bad news after all.
Name Day stows his knife and returns to the corner.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Hooray! New friends joining Typhon's legion!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: An Eagle Scout and the phony captain. Ha, never thought I'd be happy to see you again.
Regulus and Sotheby welcome the new survivors with a burst of enthusiasm.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Wow! This is a lot more people than I'd even hoped for.
The staff shuffle between different storage areas, doing their best to avoid unexpected dangers.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Don't touch anything on the shelves, people. Everything's totally harmless, just as long as you leave them be.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Please do as she says. Latham already wastes eight hours a day keeping all these knick-knacks in order. Let's not make it any more.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Then I wonder what exactly you do here, Ms. Recoleta?

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Oh, Ms. Butterfly! It's great to see you again.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: I've been working on a sequel to The Turquoise Serpent Club. Though, being stuck in a building with nothing but gray-and-white checkers to look at isn't exactly inspiring.

items.speaker: Recoleta
items.text: Oh, right, how have you been? Any new adventures to share?
The survivors find themselves with new companions to chat with.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Ms. Stranger stays by the entrance, unsure of just how to deal with Regulus's enthusiasm.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Ms. Stranger, I'm glad to see you're alright.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Perhaps you'd like an update on our current situation?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It would be much appreciated.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: Follow me. Regulus, could you give us a minute?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ah? And just when I thought we were bonding. Ah, go on then, plan whatever plans you're gonna plan. Just don't you dare leave me out of them!
Druvis leads Ms. Stranger aside. Jars line the cabinet behind them, each filled with specimens taken from arcane creatures.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: We've lost contact with the Committee Building. All we're getting are small snippets of information from survivors as they make their way here.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: It appears their attack is focused there, so we've avoided them so far. That said, we shouldn't wait around to be discovered.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: In better news, I've found a method to contact the LSCC.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: How? I thought all our signals were being jammed.
Druvis pulls out an incubator nurturing a plant.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: This is a Chattercap I found on the shelf. It can communicate messages to all its symbionts.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: And the Containment Department's logs show that Director Ezra happened to borrow one of these symbionts, taking it to Laplace.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: I've awakened this one, and fortunately, it managed to build a connection with its symbiont there. The signal is unstable, but at least we're no longer alone.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I wonder what the situation is like over there.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: I hear voices coming from that mushroom again.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Yes, but it doesn't sound like Ms. Druvis. They're asking about Laplace's current situation.

items.speaker: Ulrich
items.text: Right now? We're doing all we can to hold out. Researcher Hissabeth has formulated a plan to stop the Manus, though.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: That's right. Ask the lady on the line how she feels about getting blasted into the sky by an exploding "Fire Salamander" fuel tank from the Uranus-4 rocket.

items.speaker: Pointer
items.text: Hissabeth seems confident that Laplace's security doors are strong enough to withstand the explosion and that her firepower should provide just enough cover to allow the Foundation to rescue her team. I'll speak with her, if she's still inclined to listen.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: In summation, things are about as expected there.
At some point, Marguerite makes her way over. She peruses the specimens in the storage cabinets behind them.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Those lab geeks should be just fine as long as Hissabeth gives up her plan.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Hm. Hissabeth? Give up? Listen to yourself.
Ultimately, nothing on these shelves suits the cold-eyed woman.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: It may be best for me to share my intel on Manus Vindictae with all of you. Rules and regulations would only hold us back at this moment.

items.speaker: Druvis III
items.text: You read my mind, Ms. Stranger. I think we deserve to know.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Allow me to start with a list of the Manus's high-level figures and their basic information.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: We can't be sure just how many of them are part of this attack, but if you run into any of them, please be extra careful.
